title: Hitachi Energy

{{short description|Technology company}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2024}} {{Infobox company | name = Hitachi Energy | logo = Hitachi logo.svg | former_name = Hitachi-ABB Power Grids | industry = [[Energy industry|Energy technology]] | predecessor = Hitachi Power Solutions Co. Ltd., | founded = {{Start date|1960}} | hq_location_city = [[Zurich, Switzerland]] | key_people = Andreas Schierenbeck ([[Chief executive officer|CEO]])
Ismo Haka ([[CFO]])
Gerhard Salge ([[Chief technology officer|CTO]]) | num_employees = 58,000 | revenue = {{US$|16 billion|link=yes}} (2024) | website = {{URL|https://www.hitachienergy.com}} | footnotes = }} '''Hitachi Energy Ltd.''' is a technology company headquartered in [[Zurich]], Switzerland. The company's products include high-voltage equipment, transformers, and services for [[renewable energy]]. The company is a subsidiary of multinational conglomerate [[Hitachi|Hitachi Ltd]]. The company was formerly known as Hitachi ABB Power Grids, following a joint venture with Hitachi Ltd. and [[ABB]] Power Grids in 2014{{Cite news |title=abb-and-hitachi-to-form-strategic-power-grid-partnership-for-hvdc-in-japan |url=https://new.abb.com/news/detail/13796/abb-and-hitachi-to-form-strategic-power-grid-partnership-for-hvdc-in-japan}}, Hitachi Power solutions Co. Ltd was established in 1960 which has been integrated with Hitachi ABB Power Grids and entire stake was acquired by Hitachi from ABB and was rebranded in 2021 as Hitachi Energy Ltd. == History == === Predecessor companies and formation === {{See also|ABB}} In July 2020, following an agreement signed in 2018, [[ABB]] sold 80.1% of its Power Grids division to [[Hitachi|Hitachi Ltd.]] The resulting joint venture began operating as '''Hitachi ABB Power Grids'''.{{Cite web |title=Hitachi makes Hitachi Energy a wholly owned subsidiary for 218 billion yen and acquires shares from ABB |url=https://www.bloomberg.co.jp/news/articles/2022-09-30/RJ0ETBDWLU6801 |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=www.bloomberg.co.jp}} In October 2021, Hitachi ABB Power Grids changed its company name to Hitachi Energy. In December 2022, it was confirmed that [[Hitachi]] acquired the remaining 19.9 percent shares from [[ABB]] Ltd.{{Cite news |title=Hitachi complete Acquisition of ABB Power Grids |work=www.greentechmedia.com/ |url=https://www.greentechmedia.com/articles/read/hitachi-completes-acquisition-of-abb-power-grids |access-date=2020-05-01}} == Notable projects == Hitachi was one of the key players in the HVDC segment in Japan even before the spinoff from ABB. Some of the Notable projects include [[Kii Channel HVDC system|Kii Channel HVDC]] (2000), [[Shin-Shinano Frequency Converter|Shin Shiano Frequency Converter]] (1977), [[HVDC Hokkaido–Honshu]] (1979) are some of the classic examples of Hitachi's contribution in [[High-voltage direct current|LCC technology]] prior to the acquisition of ABB Power Grids division but their market mostly remain within Japan. Post acquisition and integration with the Energy division of Hitachi Power Solutions{{Cite web |title=Company Profile : Hitachi Power Solutions Co.,Ltd. : Hitachi |url=https://www.hitachi-power-solutions.com/en/company/index.html |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=www.hitachi-power-solutions.com}} and then, the market expanded globally as Hitachi Energy.{{Cite web |title=1400 MW Kii channel hvdc - Hitachi 2000 |url=https://www.hitachi.com/ICSFiles/afieldfile/2004/06/08/r2001_03_111.pdf |url-status=live [[transmission line]] in China, the world’s first transmission line operating at 1,100 kV voltage (2018){{Cite web |last=Molly |date=2019-03-06 |title=China's mega transmission lines greenhouse gas [[Sulfur hexafluoride|sulphur hexafluoride]] for National Grid in Kent, UK (2021){{Cite news |date=2021-12-10 |title=Hitachi Energy Partners with National Grid on World's First
